tasks.name: Compact home office
tasks.prompt: Create a 4 m × 3 m home office. Place one desk against a wall, one office chair facing the desk, and one bookshelf along another wall. Use default RF materials.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: placing the chair clipping into the desk produces collision overlaps that fail RT path computation. Right: position the chair centroid 0.4–0.6 m in front of the desk's long edge, leaving sit-down clearance.

tasks.name: Single bedroom
tasks.prompt: Create a 4 m × 3.5 m single bedroom. Place one single bed (1 m × 2 m) against a long wall, one nightstand beside the bed, and one dresser along the opposite wall. Default RF materials.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: putting the nightstand on the wall side of the bed where there is no clearance produces overlap with the bed; right: place the nightstand on the door-side of the bed with 0.05–0.1 m gap.

tasks.name: Reading nook
tasks.prompt: Create a 3 m × 3 m reading nook. Include one armchair, one floor lamp, and one side table arranged so the lamp is within 0.6 m of the armchair. Default materials.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: placing the floor lamp at the room centroid leaves the chair too far from light; right: place the lamp behind or to the side of the armchair within 0.6 m so reading light reaches the chair.

tasks.name: Small kitchenette
tasks.prompt: Create a 4 m × 3 m kitchenette. Place an L-arrangement of one kitchen counter (2 m × 0.6 m), one refrigerator (0.7 m × 0.7 m), and one sink unit (0.6 m × 0.6 m) along two adjacent walls. Default materials.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: the refrigerator placed in front of the counter blocks workflow and overlaps the counter footprint; right: align counter, sink, and fridge along two adjacent walls forming an L so each appliance sits flush against a wall.

tasks.name: Music practice room
tasks.prompt: Create a 4 m × 3 m music practice room. Place one upright piano (1.5 m × 0.6 m) flush against a wall, one piano bench in front of it, and one music stand to the right of the bench. Default materials.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: putting the piano in the middle of the room makes the bench overlap the piano keyboard area; right: place the piano against the long wall and the bench 0.4–0.5 m in front of the keyboard.

tasks.name: Childs bedroom
tasks.prompt: Create a 4 m × 3.5 m childs bedroom. Place one bunk bed (1 m × 2 m) along a wall, one dresser, and one toy chest near the foot of the bunk bed. Default materials.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: stacking the toy chest where it blocks the bunk-bed ladder breaks egress; right: leave 0.6 m clear in front of the ladder side of the bunk bed.

tasks.name: Walk-in closet
tasks.prompt: Create a 3 m × 3 m walk-in closet. Place one clothing rack (1.5 m × 0.5 m) along a long wall, one shoe shelf (1 m × 0.4 m) along an adjacent wall, and one ottoman in the centre. Default materials.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: placing the ottoman in front of the clothing rack blocks access; right: leave 0.5–0.7 m clearance in front of the rack and put the ottoman in the open quadrant.

tasks.name: Small dining room
tasks.prompt: Create a 4 m × 4 m dining room with one round dining table (1.2 m diameter) centred in the room and four matching chairs arranged at 90° around it. Default materials.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: pushing the table against a wall removes seating clearance on one side; right: centre the table so 0.6 m clearance is available for chairs on all four sides.

tasks.name: Guest room
tasks.prompt: Create a 4 m × 4 m guest room. Place one queen bed (1.5 m × 2 m) against a wall, one wardrobe along the opposite wall, and one luggage rack between them by the foot of the bed. Default materials.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: putting the luggage rack at the head of the bed blocks the nightstand area; right: place the luggage rack at the foot of the bed against the wall with 0.4 m clearance.

tasks.name: Mudroom
tasks.prompt: Create a 3 m × 2.5 m mudroom. Place one bench (1 m × 0.4 m), one coat rack on a perpendicular wall, and one shoe rack (0.8 m × 0.3 m) under the bench wall. Default materials.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: a coat rack on the same wall as the bench prevents wall-hung coats from clearing the seated bench occupant; right: place the coat rack on a wall perpendicular to the bench.

tasks.name: Reception desk area
tasks.prompt: Create a 4 m × 3.5 m reception area. Place one reception desk (1.6 m × 0.7 m) facing the entry, one receptionist chair behind it, and one waiting bench (1.5 m × 0.5 m) along the wall opposite the entry. Default materials.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: putting the waiting bench behind the reception desk hides waiting guests; right: place the bench along the wall opposite the entry so guests are visible from the desk.

tasks.name: Hobby crafts room
tasks.prompt: Create a 4 m × 3 m crafts room. Place one craft table (1.5 m × 0.7 m) in the centre, one supply cabinet (1 m × 0.4 m) along a wall, and one craft stool tucked under the long side of the craft table. Default materials.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: pushing the supply cabinet flush against the craft table creates overlap and blocks one workspace edge; right: keep the cabinet against a wall with 0.4–0.6 m walkway clearance.

tasks.name: Library
tasks.prompt: Create a 5 m × 4 m home library. Place three bookshelves (1 m × 0.3 m each) along one long wall, one reading chair facing them, and one side table within 0.6 m of the chair. Default materials.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: orienting bookshelves perpendicular to the wall blocks browsing access; right: align all three bookshelves flush against the long wall so each one is readable from the centre of the room.

tasks.name: Yoga studio
tasks.prompt: Create a 4 m × 4 m yoga studio. Place one yoga mat rack (1 m × 0.4 m) along one wall, one full-length wall mirror on an adjacent wall, and one meditation bench against the wall opposite the mirror. Default materials.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: placing the meditation bench in front of the mirror obscures the practitioner's reflection; right: keep the mirror wall clear and place the bench on the far wall.
assertions: expect expected_furniture=['yoga mat rack', 'wall mirror', 'meditation bench']

tasks.name: Server closet
tasks.prompt: Create a 3 m × 3 m server closet. Place one server rack (0.6 m × 0.8 m) at the back wall centred, one KVM cart (0.5 m × 0.5 m) along a side wall, and one step ladder in a corner. Default materials.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: placing the KVM cart directly in front of the server rack blocks cable access; right: keep ≥0.7 m clearance in front of the rack and place the KVM cart against a perpendicular wall.

tasks.name: Breakroom
tasks.prompt: Create a 4 m × 4 m office breakroom. Place one round table (1.2 m diameter) centred, four chairs around the table, and one vending machine flush against a wall. Default materials.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: placing the vending machine in the centre of the room takes the prime gathering spot; right: put the vending machine flush against a wall and centre the table for seating.

tasks.name: Examination room
tasks.prompt: Create a 4 m × 3 m medical examination room. Place one exam table (1.8 m × 0.7 m) along the long wall, one doctor stool beside it, and one supply cart against the opposite wall. Default materials.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: positioning the supply cart at the head of the exam table blocks doctor access from above; right: keep the head of the exam table clear and the supply cart on the opposite wall within reach.

tasks.name: Photo studio
tasks.prompt: Create a 4 m × 4 m small photo studio. Place one backdrop stand (2 m × 0.3 m) along the back wall, one light stand at 60° to the backdrop, and one tripod stool for the photographer. Default materials.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: putting the light stand directly between the camera and the backdrop creates a hotspot; right: angle the light at 30–60° from the camera-subject axis.

tasks.name: Drying room
tasks.prompt: Create a 3 m × 3 m laundry/drying room. Place one drying rack (1 m × 0.5 m), one washing machine (0.6 m × 0.6 m), and one dryer (0.6 m × 0.6 m) side-by-side along one wall. Default materials.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: placing the drying rack directly over the washing machine creates clearance issues for loading; right: place the rack on a perpendicular wall with ≥0.7 m clearance to washer/dryer doors.

tasks.name: Small lab
tasks.prompt: Create a 5 m × 4 m lab. Place one workbench (2 m × 0.7 m) along a long wall, one lab stool in front of the bench, and one fume hood (1 m × 0.7 m) on the perpendicular wall. Default materials.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: placing the fume hood opposite the workbench requires crossing the room with chemicals; right: place the fume hood on a wall adjacent to the workbench so the user pivots without moving.

tasks.name: Music listening room
tasks.prompt: Create a 4 m × 4 m audiophile listening room. Place one armchair centred 2.5 m from the back wall, one hi-fi cabinet (1.2 m × 0.4 m) on the front wall, and two speaker stands flanking the cabinet 1.5 m apart. Default materials.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: placing the armchair against the back wall causes nulls in low-frequency response; right: pull the chair 0.4–0.8 m off the back wall and form an equilateral triangle with the speakers.

tasks.name: Boot room
tasks.prompt: Create a 3 m × 2.5 m boot room. Place one boot bench (1 m × 0.4 m) against a long wall, one coat rack on an adjacent wall, and one umbrella stand in a corner. Default materials.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: putting the umbrella stand in front of the boot bench blocks the seating area; right: place the umbrella stand in a corner where wet umbrellas drain onto the floor without splashing the bench.

tasks.name: Small L-shaped home office
tasks.prompt: Create an L-shaped home office. Long arm 4 m × 3 m holds one desk against the outer wall, one office chair facing it; short arm 3 m × 2 m holds one filing cabinet against an outer wall. Default materials.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: defining the L as two separate rooms with overlapping bounds at the corner produces a duplicated junction cell; right: define one polygon with six vertices that traces the L outline.
assertions: expect L-shape with long arm 4 m × 3 m and short arm 3 m × 2 m

tasks.name: L-shaped studio (kitchen + living)
tasks.prompt: Create an L-shaped studio. Long arm 5 m × 4 m is the living area with one sofa against the outer wall; short arm 3 m × 3 m is the kitchen with one kitchen counter and one stool at the counter. Default materials.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: treating the inside corner as a wall blocks line of sight between zones; right: leave the inside corner open so the L is one continuous space.
assertions: expect L-shape with long arm 5 m × 4 m and short arm 3 m × 3 m

tasks.name: L-shaped corridor with reading bench
tasks.prompt: Create an L-shaped corridor. Long arm 5 m × 2 m, short arm 3 m × 2 m. Place one reading bench at the inner corner where the two arms meet, one coat rack along the long arm wall, and one umbrella stand at the short arm endpoint. Default materials.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: placing the bench across the corridor narrows passage below code; right: place the bench flush against the inside corner so the 1 m walking lane is preserved.
assertions: expect L-shape with long arm 5 m × 2 m and short arm 3 m × 2 m

tasks.name: L-shaped bedroom + nook
tasks.prompt: Create an L-shaped bedroom. Long arm 4 m × 3 m holds one double bed, one nightstand; short arm 2 m × 2 m is a reading nook with one armchair. Default materials.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: placing the armchair facing the dead-end wall ignores the L's interior connection; right: orient the armchair to face the long arm so the occupant sees the rest of the room.
assertions: expect L-shape with long arm 4 m × 3 m and short arm 2 m × 2 m

tasks.name: L-shaped meeting + breakout
tasks.prompt: Create an L-shaped meeting space. Long arm 5 m × 3 m holds one meeting table, six chairs; short arm 3 m × 3 m is a breakout with one lounge sofa, one coffee table. Default materials.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: aligning the breakout sofa toward the dead-end wall hides participants from the meeting; right: angle the sofa toward the L's inside corner so breakout occupants can rejoin the meeting.
assertions: expect L-shape with long arm 5 m × 3 m and short arm 3 m × 3 m

tasks.name: L-shaped garage workshop
tasks.prompt: Create an L-shaped garage workshop. Long arm 6 m × 4 m holds one workbench, one tool chest; short arm 4 m × 3 m holds one parts shelving. Default materials.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: pushing the tool chest into the inside corner makes drawers unreachable; right: place the tool chest flush against the long arm's outer wall with 1 m clearance for drawer pull.
assertions: expect L-shape with long arm 6 m × 4 m and short arm 4 m × 3 m

tasks.name: Two-zone office with full-height partition
tasks.prompt: Create a 10 m × 6 m office split by one full-height interior partition wall (drywall) into two equal 5 m × 6 m zones. Each zone holds one desk and one office chair. Default RF materials.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: defining the partition as a thin floating segment without joining to the perimeter walls leaves gaps at the wall junctions; right: have the partition span the full 6 m depth and join both perimeter walls.
assertions: expect overall room dims 10 m × 6 m
expect exactly one interior partition wall

tasks.name: Classroom partitioned for two grades
tasks.prompt: Create a 12 m × 6 m classroom with one interior partition (drywall) dividing it into two 6 m × 6 m zones. Each zone has one teacher desk and one student table. Default materials.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: placing the teacher desks back-to-back at the partition creates direct sound bleed; right: place each teacher desk on the outer wall of its zone so the partition isolates the two groups.
assertions: expect overall room dims 12 m × 6 m
expect exactly one interior partition wall

tasks.name: Studio with kitchenette partition

tasks.distractor: Wrong: making the partition full-height defeats the studio's open feel and changes RF propagation; right: limit partition height to 1.2 m so air and signals couple over the top.

expect exactly one interior partition wall

tasks.name: Open office with cubicle wall
tasks.prompt: Create a 8 m × 6 m open office with one cubicle partition (1.5 m tall, fabric panel) creating a private 3 m × 6 m alcove with one desk, one chair, and one filing cabinet; the open 5 m × 6 m area has one collaboration table. Default materials.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: extending the cubicle partition all the way to the ceiling violates open-office plan; right: keep partition at 1.5 m so it provides visual privacy but preserves shared ceiling.

tasks.name: Restaurant with kitchen partition
tasks.prompt: Create a 10 m × 6 m restaurant space with one full-height kitchen partition (drywall + stainless steel side) creating a 4 m × 6 m kitchen with one cooking range, one prep table, and a 6 m × 6 m dining area with one dining table and one chair. Default materials.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: omitting the partition lets kitchen heat and noise bleed to diners; right: full-height partition with stainless steel cladding on the kitchen side reflects heat back into the cooking area.

tasks.name: Lab with biosafety partition

tasks.name: Home gym with mirror partition
tasks.prompt: Create a 6 m × 5 m home gym with one half-height partition (1.5 m tall, mirror-fronted on the workout side) creating a 4 m × 5 m workout zone with one treadmill, one weight rack, and a 2 m × 5 m equipment storage zone with one storage shelf. Default materials.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: making the partition full-height encloses the storage zone and traps moisture; right: keep partition at 1.5 m so air circulates and the mirror serves the workout zone.

expect exactly one interior partition wall

tasks.name: Workshop split storage/work zones
tasks.prompt: Create a 8 m × 5 m workshop with one full-height interior partition (drywall) creating a 5 m × 5 m work zone with one workbench, one tool chest, and a 3 m × 5 m storage zone with one parts shelving. Default materials.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: not partitioning the storage area lets sawdust contaminate finished work; right: full-height partition with a sliding door isolates storage dust from active work.

tasks.name: Living room with wood floor and glass door
tasks.prompt: Create a 5 m × 4 m living room. Floor material is hardwood, walls are drywall, one wall has a 2 m × 2.1 m glass sliding door (glass). Place one sofa, one coffee table, one TV stand. Use the three RF materials hardwood / drywall / glass.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: assigning the same default material to floor, walls, and door collapses three distinct propagation surfaces into one; right: assign hardwood, drywall, and glass separately so each surface contributes its own reflection coefficient.

tasks.name: Bathroom with tile floor and ceramic walls
tasks.prompt: Create a 3 m × 2.5 m bathroom. Floor material is ceramic tile, walls are ceramic tile (wet area), one mirror is mounted on a wall. Place one toilet, one sink unit, one bathtub. Use the two RF materials ceramic / mirror.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: treating the mirror as a wall surface skips its specular reflection; right: declare the mirror as a separate material with metal-equivalent reflectivity.
assertions: expect overall room dims 3 m × 2.5 m
expect at least 2 distinct RF materials

tasks.name: Kitchen with quartz counter and metal appliances
tasks.prompt: Create a 4 m × 3.5 m kitchen. Floor is wood, walls are drywall, counter top is quartz, one refrigerator and one oven have stainless steel fronts. Place one kitchen counter, one refrigerator, one oven, one dishwasher. Use the four RF materials wood / drywall / quartz / metal.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: lumping appliances under one 'metal' tag ignores their distinct sizes for shadowing; right: each appliance gets its own object with material metal so RT tracks each one individually.

tasks.name: Office with carpet and metal door
tasks.prompt: Create a 4 m × 3 m office. Floor is carpet, walls are drywall, the door is metal. Place one desk, one chair, one bookshelf. Use the three RF materials carpet / drywall / metal.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: declaring the metal door inside the drywall material list collapses two surfaces; right: door object has material metal and is co-located with the perimeter wall but materially distinct.

tasks.name: Music room with cork floor and foam panels
tasks.prompt: Create a 4 m × 3 m music room. Floor is cork, walls are drywall with acoustic foam panels on two walls (foam material). Place one upright piano, one piano bench, one music stand. Use the three RF materials cork / drywall / foam.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: applying foam to the entire wall surface eliminates flutter echo but also wipes out high-frequency reflections; right: foam covers ~30% of wall area, leaving drywall exposed elsewhere.
assertions: expect overall room dims 4 m × 3 m
expect at least 3 distinct RF materials

tasks.name: Gym with rubber floor and mirror wall
tasks.prompt: Create a 5 m × 4 m home gym. Floor is rubber, walls are drywall except one wall is fully mirror (mirror material). Place one treadmill, one weight bench, one dumbbell rack. Use the three RF materials rubber / drywall / mirror.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: declaring the mirror wall as drywall ignores its strong specular reflection; right: declare it as a mirror material so RT models the spec reflection lobe.
assertions: expect overall room dims 5 m × 4 m
expect at least 3 distinct RF materials

tasks.name: Photo studio with vinyl floor and blackout curtains
tasks.prompt: Create a 5 m × 4 m photo studio. Floor is vinyl, walls are drywall painted white, one wall has blackout curtains (fabric material). Place one backdrop stand, one light stand, one tripod stool. Use the three RF materials vinyl / drywall / fabric.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: treating curtains as drywall ignores their high-frequency absorption; right: curtains declared as fabric with low reflectivity.
assertions: expect overall room dims 5 m × 4 m
expect at least 3 distinct RF materials

tasks.name: Lab with epoxy floor and FRP walls
tasks.prompt: Create a 5 m × 4 m lab. Floor is epoxy, walls are fiberglass-reinforced plastic (FRP), one wall has a glass observation window. Place one workbench, one fume hood, one lab stool. Use the three RF materials epoxy / FRP / glass.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: omitting the glass window in materials makes the wall look uniform to RT; right: declare the window as a distinct glass region within the FRP wall.
assertions: expect overall room dims 5 m × 4 m

tasks.name: Server closet with raised floor and metal door
tasks.prompt: Create a 3 m × 3 m server closet. Floor is a raised access floor (metal panels above plenum), walls are drywall, door is metal. Place one server rack, one KVM cart, one cable tray. Use the three RF materials metal / drywall / cable.

assertions: expect overall room dims 3 m × 3 m
expect at least 3 distinct RF materials

tasks.name: Library with hardwood floor and oak shelves
tasks.prompt: Create a 5 m × 4 m home library. Floor is hardwood, walls are drywall, three bookshelves are solid oak (wood material distinct from floor hardwood). Place three bookshelves, one reading chair, one side table. Use the three RF materials hardwood / drywall / wood.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: collapsing hardwood floor and oak shelves into one wood material ignores their geometric difference; right: keep hardwood as a horizontal slab and oak as vertical shelving — both wood but at different surface orientations.

expect at least 3 distinct RF materials

tasks.name: IRC-compliant bedroom
tasks.prompt: Create a 4 m × 4 m bedroom (room_type='bedroom'). Add one window on a perimeter wall, sized so its area is at least 8% of the floor area (1.28 m²); 1.2 m × 1.2 m suffices. Place one double bed, one nightstand, one wardrobe. Default RF materials.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: placing the window on the interior wall (no exterior view) violates IRC §R303 perimeter requirement; right: window goes on north/south/east/west perimeter wall.
assertions: expect single habitable room of type 'bedroom'
expect total window aperture >= 1.28 m^2 (8% of floor)
expect all windows on perimeter walls (north/south/east/west)

tasks.name: IRC-compliant living room (two windows)

assertions: expect single habitable room of type 'living'
expect total window aperture >= 1.60 m^2 (8% of floor)
expect all windows on perimeter walls (north/south/east/west)

assertions: expect single habitable room of type 'kitchen'
expect total window aperture >= 0.96 m^2 (8% of floor)
expect all windows on perimeter walls (north/south/east/west)

expect total window aperture >= 0.96 m^2 (8% of floor)

tasks.name: Move the sofa (apartment)
tasks.prompt: Take the pre-shipped apartment scene_state.json. Move the sofa from its current position to be flush against the opposite living-room wall. Preserve all other objects and materials.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: writing a fresh scene_state.json from scratch loses the apartment's existing room polygons and other furniture; right: load the pre-shipped JSON, mutate only the sofa's position fields, and re-dump.

Add two new drywall partitions to demarcate the zones. Remove any existing pallets or racking. Floor stays existing material; walls drywall.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: dropping new furniture without removing the existing pallets produces collisions; right: explicitly delete pallet/racking records first, then add partitions, then add new furniture.
assertions: expect output scene_state.json reflects the requested structural edit
expect 3 zones (collab + focus + amenities) each ~1/3 of warehouse area
expect new furniture: collab table + 6 chairs + 4 desks + 4 chairs + kitchenette + 2 standing tables

tasks.name: Convert apartment to open-plan studio
tasks.prompt: Take the pre-shipped apartment scene_state.json. Convert it into a single open-plan studio: remove all interior partitions (living/kitchen/bedroom dividers stay only between bathroom and main space). Union the remaining room polygons into one big living zone. Preserve the bathroom and its partition; preserve all furniture except move the bed into one corner of the new open zone.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: removing the bathroom wall too creates an open toilet — violation of dignity and building code; right: preserve the bathroom enclosure and only union the bedroom/living/kitchen polygons.
assertions: expect output scene_state.json reflects the requested structural edit
expect all interior partitions removed EXCEPT bathroom enclosure
expect remaining rooms (living + kitchen + bedroom) unioned into single open zone
expect bathroom and its walls preserved
expect bed moved into a corner of the new open zone
